title: Federal Reserve Board - Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
主要内容: On December 12, 2012, the Federal Reserve issued an FOMC statement, noting that economic activity and employment continued to expand at a moderate pace, despite weather disruptions. The unemployment rate had declined slightly since the summer but remained elevated. Household spending advanced, and the housing sector improved, though business investment growth slowed. Inflation remained below the Committee’s longer-run objective, except for temporary energy-related fluctuations. Longer-term inflation expectations remained stable. The Fed announced it would continue purchasing agency mortgage-backed securities at $40 billion monthly and start buying longer-term Treasury securities at $45 billion monthly starting in January. The central bank aimed to maintain downward pressure on interest rates and support mortgage markets, while monitoring economic developments and continuing purchases if labor market conditions did not improve significantly. The Fed kept the federal funds rate target range at 0 to 1/4 percent, based on the expectation that the low range would remain appropriate as long as the unemployment rate remained above 6.5 percent. Longer-term inflation expectations remained well anchored.
